title: The $4 million lottery ticket — Part 2
style: Warm painterly 2D cartoon illustration, cinematic graphic-novel look: clean bold dark outlines, rich textured digital painting, soft volumetric light, deep warm oranges and moody blues, detailed environment, vertical 9:16 composition.
character: MAIN CHARACTER: a lanky ADULT man drawn as a minimalist cartoon: a perfectly round smooth tan head, two tiny solid black dot eyes set wide apart, short thin eyebrow strokes, a very small simple mouth, no nose, no visible hair, simple long limbs, dark charcoal baseball cap, oversized heather-grey hoodie, black slim pants, white sneakers. Minimal face like a webcomic, not a child, not anime, no big eyes.

scenes.A: Night, the man at a rainy bus stop dialing his phone, holding the lottery ticket, streetlight glow.
scenes.B: An elderly woman with grey hair and a cardigan opening the door of a small cozy house, surprised, warm light behind her, the man on the porch holding out the ticket.
scenes.C: The elderly woman crying happy tears and hugging the man on her porch, rain stopping, warm light.
scenes.D: Weeks later, the man opening a handwritten envelope at his kitchen table, a check inside with no readable text, sunlight.
scenes.E: Close-up portrait of the man facing the viewer, moved and smiling, kitchen window light behind him.

segments.text: She answers on the first ring. She's been crying. That ticket was her late husband's numbers.
Same numbers. Every week. For thirty-one years.
You hand it back. She doesn't let go of your hand.
Three weeks later, an envelope shows up at your door.
A thank-you note. And a check for one hundred thousand dollars. She insisted.
Four million would have been yours to lose. This was yours to keep. The end.
